Factor the numerator in Quantity A as a difference of squares:

$$x^2-1=(x-1)(x+1).$$

Then, since $x\ne1$, the denominator $x-1$ is not zero, so you can cancel the common factor:

$$\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}
=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1}
=x+1.$$

That is exactly Quantity B, so **the two quantities are equal (C)**.
